items.item_text: ARRT (American Registry of Radiologic Technologist) Certification
American Heart Association (AHA) or American Red Cross Basic Life Support (BLS), or UC Davis Health CPR
IV Certification within six months of hire
Ability to use basic nursing skills and CPR
Demonstrated experience and ability to operate CT equipment to provide quality images.
Experience performing similar duties in a trauma setting desired.
Contrast administration experience

The CT Technologist is responsible for performing a variety of diagnostic imaging procedures using CT equipment to aid in patient diagnosis and treatment. This role operates CT control consoles, positions patients, and ensures high-quality imaging, while adhering to radiation safety protocols and quality control measures.

The technologist prepares and administers contrast media, assists radiologists in guided procedures, and maintains equipment cleanliness and readiness. Additionally, the position requires patient interaction, ensuring understanding of procedures and addressing any concerns. The technologist also contributes to departmental functions, including process improvements, equipment maintenance, and maintaining a clean, organized work environment.
Valid California Radiologic Technologist (CRT) required
American Registry of Radiologic Technologist ARRT(R) or ARRT(R)(CT)
ARRT (CT) within six months of hire
Must be able to adapt to new programs and equipment upgrades as the radiological field advances.
Must be a self-starter requiring minimal direction from supervisor or physicians.
Knowledge and ability to operate radiology equipment, such as different CT equipment, and auxiliary equipment to provide quality images.
Knowledge and ability to fill out departmental and hospital report forms and records.
Comprehensive knowledge of radiology principles and practices including anatomy and physiology, radiation protection and physics, radiographic positioning, surgical and nursing procedures.
Knowledge of UCH Hospital and Department Policies and Procedures.
Ability to function and remain calm under multiple direction and/or fluctuations of work volume.
Ability to handle a high patient volume in a high-pressure department with constantly changing priorities.
Ability to remain flexible with scheduling changes throughout day to accommodate patient care needs.
Skill to communicate clearly and effectively on the telephone, in person and written document.
Skill to organize workload by priority to produce a sufficient volume of work in a timely manner.
Ability to react quickly and knowledgeably in emergency situations.
Ability to display common sense and good judgement in following rules, protocols, policies and procedures.
Ability to perform on an independent level, using initiative and ingenuity to assist the Radiologist in achieving a diagnosis.
Demonstrated ability to effectively manage multiple priorities in a complex, challenging environment.
Demonstrates adaptability and flexibility, anticipates, and effectively handles change.
Organizational skills to establish workload priorities for completion of all tasks in a timely manner.
Organizational skills to coordinate and complete workload with high degree of accuracy.
Must have knowledge of Joint Commission requirements, Title 17 law, and hospital policies and procedures.
Ability and skills to be sensitive and professional with patients, physicians, and staff in relations and appearance.
